text:
name: read_aloud
does: Reads the text on the screen out loud, can cast the sound to a speaker, and keeps a volume cap so it is never too loud.
inputs: the page or message to read, which speaker to use, and how fast to read; hot items such as new alerts are read first
people say:
- Can you read this page to me?
- I can't see the words very well, say them out loud
- Read my new messages, please
- Play this article through the kitchen speaker
- My eyes are tired, talk me through this email
- Slower, please, I can't follow

Yuki ran a small flower shop and she never slept well. Last night a hot wind blew through her bedroom window, and the baby next door began to cry at three in the morning. By dawn she was tired and cross.

"Hey assistant," she said, rubbing her eyes. "I want to nap this afternoon. Wake me up next Tuesday at noon... no, sorry, I mean today at one. Just a short rest before the shop gets busy."

The assistant said it had set an alarm for one o'clock today and asked if she wanted it to turn on the fan. Yuki said yes. It switched the fan on low and told her the alarm was ready. She smiled, closed the shop sign, and lay down.

Ishaan sat in his parked car with a cup of tea going cold in the holder. His daily shift started in twenty minutes, and he did not want to climb out of the cab again until night. He picked up his phone and typed in a hurry.

"whats on at the cinma tonight near me"

The assistant understood him anyway. It found three films playing at the Grand Cinema, two miles away, and read out the times: 6:15, 7:40 and 9:05. Ishaan asked for the trailer of the middle one. The assistant played it on his phone screen, and he watched with a small smile. Then he asked it to save the 7:40 show to his calendar, and the assistant did.

When you cough in the night and look at the clock, it shows the time where you are. But the sun does not rise everywhere at once. Like a seed that sprouts a little at a time, the morning moves across the world from east to west, so a huge map is split into time zones. Each zone has its own clock. People use the clock for calls, flights and meetings. They ask things like "What time is it in Tokyo?" or "Set my clock to London time." Some say "My phone is an hour off" when they travel, or "Show me two clocks at once." The phone changes by itself when you cross into a new zone.

They want a meal plan for the week that works around a trip and wastes less food.
Plan my meals for the week, I'm away on a trip on Thursday
what shud i cook this week, less shopping pls
Make a simple dinner plan that uses what I have
I'm going on a trip Friday, so nothing that will not last in the fridge
Can you suggest five dinners for the week?
Help me eat less takeout this week
What can I make with eggs and rice for the next few days?
Could you please plan a week of easy meals for two people, because I'm going to be very busy and want to cook less?

People count days for all sorts of reasons: a birthday, a holiday, or the day a library book is due. Counting days helps you plan, and it can calm you down if you hate waiting. Even an angry person might feel better knowing there are only nine days left. Some people read a newspaper to check the date and then do the counting in their head. A phone can do it for you. People say "How many days until my birthday?", "How old am I if I was born in 1990?" or "Count the days since we moved." They can also ask for a change, like "Start from tomorrow" or "Count only the weekdays."

Sofia was not good with technology. Her granddaughter had given her a tablet, and she hated how many buttons it had. This morning she was worried because she had to help the girl with homework, and the tablet was pricey, so she did not want to break it.

"Please," she said slowly to the tablet, "tell me what homework Lina has. She has a test next Tuesday at noon."

The assistant opened the school app and read out the list. There was a math sheet due Friday, and a reading task for the test next Tuesday at noon. Sofia asked it to remind her on Monday evening. The assistant said it had set a reminder for Monday at six. Sofia felt a little proud.

Hiroshi was bored in a long Monday meeting, with his phone clipped to his belt and his laptop on mute. He decided to fix something that had bothered him for days.

"Change the password for my email," he whispered to the assistant. "No wait, not the email. The work account."

The assistant asked if he wanted a strong new password. Hiroshi said yes. It made one with letters, numbers and symbols and saved it to his password list. Then it asked if it should lock his phone after one minute, and he said yes.

Just then his boss asked him a question. "Unmute me," said Hiroshi quickly. The assistant turned on his microphone and he began to talk.

An alarm is a sound that wakes you or warns you about something. A kitchen timer is the same idea for cooking: you set it for ten minutes and it rings when the pasta is done. Most phones let you change the time, the sound, and the days the alarm repeats. People say "Wake me at six", "Snooze for five minutes" or "Cancel my alarm." Some ask for a total countdown, like "Count down from forty minutes." On the lock screen you can often see the next alarm and stop it without opening the phone. Sleepy people like this because they only want to tap once.

name: room_vacuum
does: Sends a robot vacuum to clean one room, then shows a color map of where it went after downloading the floor plan.
inputs: which room to clean, how strong the suction should be, and whether the door of the room is open
people say:
- Vacuum the living room, please
- The kitchen floor is covered in crumbs
- Can you clean the bedroom while I'm out?
- Just do the hallway, nowhere else
- Make the robot go over the carpet twice
- There's dust everywhere in the study

name: homework_reminder
does: Keeps a list of homework due dates and posts a reminder, like a pill reminder, before anything is late.
inputs: the subject, the due date, and how early the reminder should come
people say:
- Remind me about my history essay on Thursday
- I keep forgetting my science project
- Tell me the night before my math sheet is due
- What do I need to hand in this week?
- Don't let me miss the English assignment
- Warn me when something is due tomorrow

Jack the gardener was painting the garden fence on a sunny Saturday. His hands were covered in white paint, so he could not touch his phone. He wanted a neat cup of coffee, and he wanted it right now.

"Make me a coffee," he called to the kitchen speaker. "No sugar, and no milk. I don't want anything fancy."

The assistant told the coffee machine to brew one black cup, strong. A minute later it said, "Your coffee is ready." Jack also had a video call with his sister at noon. "Start the zoom call at twelve," he said, and the assistant answered that it would. Then Jack wiped his hands and went to get his drink.

Henry woke up late and his head felt heavy. His phone buzzed on the table, and he could hardly hear it over the noise from the street. He grabbed it and spoke to the assistant.

"Text my wife, tell her I'm working late tonight. Say it's honey chicken for dinner, so she should start the rice."

The assistant read the message back. Henry frowned. "No, change that. Not working late. I mean working from home. And say sorry for the mess."

The assistant fixed the message and sent it: "Hi love, I'm working from home today. I'll make honey chicken, so please start the rice. Sorry for the mess." Henry smiled and finally got out of bed.

They want the text on their screen to be bigger, so they can see it, even on holiday.
Bigger text please
I can't see this, it's too small
Make the words larger
Make the text a bit bigger. No, a lot bigger
I'm on holiday without my glasses and I have a sour feeling about this tiny print
Zoom in on the screen
My eyes are tired, can you make everything easier to read?
Could you please increase the text size, because I'm sitting far from the phone?

They want their coffee or tea made with less sugar. Some are polite, some are rushed, and some talk over the dishwasher.
Half the sugar, please
Make my tea less sweet
Listen, I only want one spoon of sugar today
Could you please make it half as sweet as yesterday?
Too sweet! Cut the sugar by half
The dishwasher is so loud, but I need my coffee with a lot less sugar
If it's not too much trouble, would you mind making my drink a little less sweet?
My last tea was twice as sweet as I like it

They want to know how many days are left until a date, like Pancake Day or a mild spring day.
How many days until Pancake Day?
days left to my birthday?
I think my trip is soon, how long do I have to wait?
Can you count down to the first day of spring?
It's getting mild outside, so is it nearly summer? How many days to go?
Tell me how many sleeps until the party
How far away is the exam, in days?
When I'm done with this winter, I want to know how long until the holiday starts

A budget is a plan for your money. You write down what comes in each month and what goes out, like rent, food and bills. It helps you save and spend less on things you don't need. Being careful matters most in a cold month, when heating costs more. Many people scan their receipts so the phone can add them up. People say "How much did I spend on food?", "Set my food budget to two hundred" or "Tell me when I've spent half." They also ask for changes such as "Move fifty to savings." The plan is not fixed, so you can change it any time.

name: parking_timer
does: Starts a countdown when parking begins and warns the driver before the ticket ends, so they can run back to the car in time.
inputs: where the car is, when parking began, and how long the ticket lasts; it gives steady updates until the time is up
people say:
- How long do I have left on my spot?
- Tell me before my parking runs out
- I need to be back at the car by four
- Did I pay for two hours or three?
- Don't let me get a ticket
- I just parked, keep an eye on the time

Person: Can you move my dentist appointment? I don't want it on Friday.
Assistant: Sure. What day would you like instead?
Person: Hold on a moment, my room is still dim and I can't see my notes.
Assistant: Take your time.
Person: Make it Monday morning, but not before ten.
Assistant: Monday has a free slot at 10:30. Should I write it in?
Person: Yes, please write it in.
Assistant: Done. Your dentist appointment is now Monday at 10:30.

It was a foggy morning in July, and Ben, a retired teacher, was making tea when the kettle slipped. A little hot water splashed on his finger. It stung, but he stayed calm.

"Assistant, what do I do for a burn on my finger?" he asked.

The assistant told him to hold it under cool running water for ten minutes.

"Wait, it's not the finger," said Ben. "It's my palm. Does that change anything?"

The assistant said no, the same steps were fine for the palm, but if the skin turned white or blistered badly, he should see a doctor. It also set a ten minute timer. Ben stood at the sink until it rang. "Thank you," he said.

Person: Start a timer for our board game.
Assistant: Sure. How long should each turn be?
Person: seventy seconds. I bought this game at the market and nobody knows the rules.
Assistant: Okay, a seventy second timer is ready. Do you want it to repeat each turn?
Person: Yes, and clear the old scores too.
Assistant: I can't keep scores for that game, but I can start the timer. Do you want a small chime when time is up?
Person: Yes, a small one. We are only four people.
Assistant: Good. The timer is running.

They want to know the weather in the hills before a camping trip. Black clouds could cut the trip short, and the tent wire is already packed.
What's the weather up in the hills?
Will it rain on the trail this weekend?
The sky over the hills looks bad, should I bother packing the tent?
Is it going to be windy up there tonight?
How cold does it get on the hill at night?
It's freezing even down here, what will the hills be like?
I'm leaving for the trail at six, will I need a rain jacket?
Could you please check the hill forecast, because my kids are coming and I don't want them to get cold?

They want the blinds opened to let in soft morning light, before they stretch and eat their noodle breakfast.
open the blinds
let some light in
blinds up pls
open the blinds half way, its too brigt
I can't see a thing in here, can you do something about the window?
Pull up the blinds in the kitchen
Could you please open the living room blinds? I'd like some soft light while I have my breakfast
It's so dark in here, let the sun in

Person: Turn on do not disturb and make my screen dimmer.
Assistant: Sure. How long should do not disturb stay on?
Person: Until three. Don't forget to turn it off then.
Assistant: I won't. May I ask how dim you want the screen?
Person: Make it a warm, creamy color, like night mode. I've just finished a long shift.
Assistant: Done. Do not disturb is on until three, and night mode is on at low brightness.
Person: Thanks. Can you also turn the volume down?
Assistant: Yes. The volume is now at one quarter.

A workout is a plan for moving your body. It is made of exercises, which you repeat in sets and reps. For example, ten push-ups is one set of ten reps. Rest days matter too, because muscles grow when you stop. If you skip rest, tired muscles can lead to dangerous injuries. After a hard weekend in a tent in the hills, you might want an easy day. People say "Start a ten minute workout", "Add one more set" or "Give me a rest day on Wednesday." They also say "Make it easier" or "Do fewer reps." The plan changes as you get stronger.

Writing starts with a draft, which is a first try that does not have to be perfect. Then you edit it: you fix spelling, shorten long sentences, and check the word count. A spell checker will notice if you type tooth as tooht. People who write emails often need to reply fast, but a tall pile of messages can wait until you are ready. Writers ask things like "How many words is this?", "Fix my spelling" or "Read it back to me." They also ask for changes: "Make it shorter", "Make it sound more polite" or "Change the first line." Editing is just making your words clearer.

Do not disturb is a setting that keeps your phone quiet. Calls and messages still arrive, but the phone does not ring or buzz. It is useful at night, in class or in a meeting. You can schedule it so it turns on and off by itself, for example from ten at night until seven in the morning. People say "Turn on do not disturb", "Schedule quiet time for the evening" or "Let my mother's calls through." Imagine working in the soil on a windy day. You may want the phone silent so a buzz does not interrupt you. When the time ends, the phone goes back to normal.

Ananya was new to the city, and her apartment was not perfect. The kitchen tap gave her water that tasted bitter, and the orange juice she made with it was no better. She thought the filter might be old.

"Hey assistant," she said, "my water filter is half used up and the water tastes bitter. Can you find someone to change it?"

The assistant searched nearby repair shops and found a plumber with good reviews, open until six. It asked if she wanted it to ring the shop. Ananya said yes. The assistant called, and the plumber promised to come the next day at ten. It then added the visit to her calendar and set a reminder for nine.

Silvia had just woken up and her cat was already batting a toy across the floor. Her head was still fuzzy, but she had a big day. She grabbed her phone and typed in a hurry.

"set a focus timer for 45 mins and adjst it to silent mode"

The assistant understood. It started a forty five minute focus timer and switched her phone to silent mode, so no sounds would break her work. When she sat down at her desk, the timer was already running. It also asked if she wanted a short break at the end. "Yes, ten minutes," Silvia typed, and the assistant added a ten minute break after the focus time.

First aid means helping someone right away when they get a small injury, before a doctor can see them. For a small cut, you wash your hands, clean the cut and cover it. For a burn, you hold it under cool water. If something gets in your eye, wash it with clean water and don't rub. Pharmacies sell plasters and cold packs, so keep a few in a box at home. Stay away from home remedies like butter on a burn. People say "What do I do for a bee sting?", "How long should I cool a burn?" or "Call an ambulance." They can also ask for a step to be repeated.

Jonah had just finished a long night shift at the hospital. He was tired and wanted to send a quick note to his sister before he slept, but he had to carry a heavy bag home first. On the bus he spoke to his phone.

"Write a short email to Dana. Say I'll visit at quarter to eight on Saturday. Check my spelling."

The assistant wrote the email and read it back. It had found one mistake and fixed it. Jonah liked how fast it was, since his speed with the keyboard was slow when he was so sleepy. He said, "Send it." The assistant sent the email to Dana, and Jonah closed his eyes.

Mei came home from the hospital after a night shift and found the printer jammed. She had a form to send before breakfast, so she typed fast.

"scan this form and email it to my boss, my printr is stuck"

The assistant opened the scanner on her phone, took a picture of the form and made a clean page with a wide margin. Then it emailed it to her boss. Mei also needed new ink. "What's the ink called?" she asked. The assistant read out the cartridge name and spelled it letter by letter, so she could write it down. It said the cartridge cost about twelve dollars at the shop on Main Street. Mei wrote it on her hand and went to sleep.

A phone call is when you talk to someone by phone. If you can't answer, the call becomes a missed call, and the person may leave a message in your voicemail. Missed calls pile up like pictures in an album, so most phones show a list. You can add a number to your contacts to see a name next time. Speakerphone lets other people nearby hear the call, which is handy when your hands are busy. People say "Call my brother", "Put him on speaker" or "Who called me?" They also ask "Add this number to my contacts" or "Play my voicemail."

They want to cancel a smoke alarm that went off by mistake, like white steam from a kettle or burnt toast, with a bucket of water nearby.
Cancel the alarm
It's a false alarm, turn it off
Stop the smoke alarm, it was only toast
Shut it up, there's no fire
The smoke alarm is going off but it's just white steam from the kettle, please cancel it
Please cancel the alert, I'm fine and nothing is burning
My kitchen alarm went off by mistake, so could you please stop it and tell the fire service not to come, because it was only cooking?
Turn off the alarm, everything is okay

Ji-woo was an office worker and her days were always busy. On Friday afternoon she was packing her bag when she broke the zipper on her jacket. She sighed and talked to her phone.

"Set an alarm for this Saturday afternoon at three. I need to call the tailor about my zipper before the shop closes."

The assistant replied that the alarm was set for Saturday at three o'clock. Ji-woo thought for a second. "Make it two thirty, so I have time to find the number." The assistant changed the alarm to two thirty and added a note: "Call the tailor." Ji-woo nodded and walked home.

Remy was in a hurry. His dad was sick in bed, and Remy had to hand in his school work before nine. He ran to the kitchen with his bag half open.

"Open my homework list," he said to the tablet. "What is due today?"

The assistant showed three items. There was a science sheet, a poem, and an essay of three hundred words. Remy groaned. "Remind me at lunch to finish the essay," he said, and the assistant set a reminder for twelve thirty. Then Remy asked it to text his teacher that his dad was sick. The assistant wrote and sent the message, and Remy grabbed his coat and ran for the bus.

Person: order me a burger and fries from tonite's usual place
Assistant: Sure. Which place do you mean? You have two saved.
Person: the one on Oak Street, my fridge is empty
Assistant: Got it. Where should it be delivered?
Person: my truck is at the depot, so deliver to the gate
Assistant: The lunch rush is at its height, so delivery may be slow, about forty minutes. Is that okay?
Person: fine
Assistant: Your order is placed. I can't add a tip yet, but you can do it when it arrives.

Money does not last forever, so many families make a plan. First you estimate how much comes in each month, then how much you need for rent, food and bills. Think of all the mouths to feed at home. If your numbers don't match, you may need to spend less on something. People say "Show me my spending this month", "Set aside twenty for savings" or "Estimate what I will spend on groceries." They also say "Spend less on coffee" or "Tell me when I'm close to my limit." A good plan is simple, and you can fix it whenever a bill is bigger than you expected.

They want to turn their social media notifications back on, so they resume getting them. Some people pause them when the phone's battery meter is low.
Turn my notifications back on
Start showing me alerts again
Resume notifications for my posts
I paused my alerts, can you undo that?
Tell me when someone likes my picture. No, only when I get a new follower
Please bring back the notifications, I need to see what people say
My battery is low, so I turned them off, but now it's charged
Unmute my account alerts

Meal planning means deciding what you will eat before you are hungry. You pick meals for the week, make a shopping list, and cook some things early. A smart plan uses leftovers: roast a chicken on Sunday, and use the rest in a sandwich on Monday. A pan with some depth is good for soups and stews. Meal plans help with packed lunches, diets and a tight budget. People say "Plan dinners for five days", "Nothing with nuts" or "Swap Tuesday's pasta for soup." They also ask "What can I cook with potatoes?" and "Make my plan cheaper."

Person: Read my unread emails.
Assistant: You have six unread emails. Should I read them all or only the new ones?
Person: just the ones from my boss. I don't want to miss anything
Assistant: Your boss sent two. The first is a note about Friday. The second has an ugly red label because it is marked urgent.
Person: Reply to the urgent one.
Assistant: What would you like to say?
Person: Say I'll call him when I stop driving.
Assistant: Done, I've sent the reply. I can't open attachments while you drive, but I can save them for later.

Rania was a gardener, and her tall husband slept badly in small hotel beds. She planned a trip for two and spoke to her phone.

"Find me a hotel for two nights in Lisbon. I want a soft bed, long enough for someone two hundred centimeters tall."

The assistant found a hotel with long beds and read out the price. Rania said, "Wait, three nights, not two. And we may miss the last train, so I need a late check-in."

The assistant changed the booking details to three nights with a late check-in at midnight. It asked her to confirm, and Rania said yes. A few seconds later, the room was held for her.

Rania was late for an invitation to her friend's party, and she ran out to her car with her keys in her hand. The seats were cold and she could see her breath.

"It's freezing in here," she said to the car assistant.

The assistant turned on the heat and the seat warmers. Rania looked at the screen. "It's so bright. Can you dim it a bit?" The assistant dimmed the display. Then it told her the tank was only half full, and showed a gas station on the way to the party. Rania smiled and said, "Take me there first, then to Sam's house." The assistant started the route.

They want to move a meeting to a later time, like the carrot cake club on Tuesday.
Move my meeting to later
Push my top meeting to the afternoon and mute its alerts
Can we do the three o'clock at four instead?
Shift the carrot cake club to six and tell everyone
Reschedule tomorrow's call to after lunch and mute the reminder
Move it back an hour
I can't make Tuesday's meeting, so please move it to Wednesday and mute the pop-ups
Put my call on hold until next week and cancel the alert

Fatou was a gardener who sold plants online. On Wednesday she was in her packing station in the shed, with shallow pots of herbs waiting to ship. But the wifi was so slow that her orders would not load.

"Why is the internet so slow?" she asked the assistant. "It's half as fast as yesterday."

The assistant checked the router and found that six devices were using it. It asked if she wanted to restart it. Fatou said yes. The router restarted, and a minute later the speed was twice as fast. The assistant also offered to pause her smart TV, and she agreed. Fatou loaded her orders and began to ship the plants.

Person: How long will it take to get to the library after school today?
Assistant: Where will you start from?
Person: I'm new here and I don't know the name. I'm at the parking meter by the big park.
Assistant: Thanks. I see the park. Are you walking or driving?
Person: driving. my son is hungry and I peeled him an orange but it won't last
Assistant: The library is twelve minutes away by car. Take the next left, then go straight for two miles.
Person: Can you tell me where he can buy food there?
Assistant: I can't see the shops inside the library, but there is a cafe next door.

Person: area please
Assistant: Of what shape? And what are the sides?
Person: square 12 centimeters
Assistant: A square with sides of twelve centimeters has an area of 144 square centimeters.
Person: forward that to my mom
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't forward messages from this chat. I can send it as a text if you give me her name.
Person: no thx
Assistant: Okay. Do you want another shape?
Person: nope

Finding a movie is easy when you know what you want. You pick a film, a cinema, and a time. Start times are listed in order, so the first show is at the top. Many cinemas have middle rows that feel best, and tickets cost more there. To know the price, you multiply the cost of one ticket by the number of people. People say "What's on tonight?", "Show me the trailer" or "Book two seats in the middle." They also ask for changes, like "Make it the later show" or "Make it three tickets." You can order snacks at some cinemas too.

Person: I would like to unlock the front door for my grandson, please. He is coming home from school and I am in the garden with a bad knee, so I can't get there quickly.
Assistant: Of course. Which door do you mean, the front door or the garage?
Person: The front. And check the doorbell, there was a man here who wanted to sell me something.
Assistant: The front door is now unlocked. The doorbell camera shows one recent visitor at 2:15, a man with a box.
Person: Can you show me his face on the doorbell channel?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't show video in this chat, but I can send it to your tablet.

Minh was a retired teacher who loved to bake bread on Sundays. This morning she wanted to try a new loaf with bay leaf and herbs, and she was worried the dough would rise too long.

"Hello assistant," she said politely. "Could you please search for a simple herb bread recipe? I would like one that takes under three hours, because my grandchildren are coming for lunch at one."

The assistant found a recipe and read out the steps. It said the dough needs one hour to rise, then forty minutes in the oven. Minh asked for hourly reminders to check the dough. The assistant said it had set a reminder every hour, and Minh began to mix the flour.
